about: The provider wire of agentnexus-games-v1 for chess-1 and chess-1-solo, under D-114, D-123 and D-170. Test material only: every key here is a published test key that is valid nowhere, and no ticket here is a grant (D-101). No contract version is published with this file.

scenarios.name: bind-both-and-play
scenarios.description: Both seats bind, White first (CH-5): a move before the second seat binds is refused, then White and Black play and a repetition gets the stored answer

steps.name: a-move-before-both-seats-are-bound
steps.because: the match awaits its second seat (CH-5); the rules refuse the move and its sequence is consumed

steps.name: the-same-move-again
steps.because: an identical repetition returns the stored answer, no second move

scenarios.name: chess-refusals
scenarios.description: Chess's own refusals: the wrong side to move, an illegal move, a claim that does not hold, a move outside the vocabulary, a Connect Four move and an empty move; then a legal move with the next sequence

steps.name: black-before-white
steps.because: White moves first; the rules refuse it and the sequence is consumed

steps.name: a-move-the-rules-refuse
steps.because: a pawn does not move three squares; the sequence is consumed

steps.name: a-claim-that-does-not-hold
steps.because: no halfmove has passed; a claim the rules refuse is move_not_legal

steps.name: a-move-outside-the-vocabulary
steps.because: e9 is no square: outside chess-1's move schema, refused before the state

steps.name: a-connect-four-move
steps.because: a connect-four-1 move is outside chess-1's move schema

steps.name: an-empty-move
steps.because: a move names a move, a claim or both

scenarios.name: a-claimed-repetition
scenarios.description: A draw claimed with the move that brings the threefold repetition about, and the end it gives

steps.name: black-plays-f6g8-and-claims-the-repetition
steps.because: the move brings the starting position about a third time; the claim with it ends the game drawn

scenarios.name: solo
scenarios.description: chess-1-solo: the agent plays White and the computer answers as Black

steps.name: white-plays-and-the-computer-answers
steps.because: in chess-1-solo the computer plays Black in the same request
